setsid fails in my environment (seccomp), confirming my shell runs under the scored-worker profile. That's why check.py can't run here — an environment limitation. My harness (without setsid) is the closest replica.

Now let me run the harness with the rlimits applied, plus the worst-case timing test under RLIMIT_AS=2GB and RLIMIT_CPU=180.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 tmp/harness.py submission/main.py 2>&1 | tail -9 && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import resource, subprocess, sys, time, os
def child_limits():
    for which, values in [(resource.RLIMIT_CPU,(180,181)),(resource.RLIMIT_AS,(2*1024**3,)*2),
        (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE,(256,256)),(resource.RLIMIT_NPROC,(64,64)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE,(64*1024**2,)*2),(resource.RLIMIT_CORE,(0,0)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_STACK,(8*1024**2,)*2),(resource.RLIMIT_MEMLOCK,(65536,65536)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE,(819200,819200)),(resource.RLIMIT_SIGPENDING,(4096,4096)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_NICE,(0,0)),(resource.RLIMIT_RTPRIO,(0,0))]:
        resource.setrlimit(which, values)
for name in ('worst','routes','rows','big'):
    data=open('/tmp/%s.json'%name,'rb').read()
    t=time.time()
    p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-B','/workspace/submission/main.py'],input=data,
                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE,preexec_fn=child_limits,
                     env=dict(os.environ,PYTHONHASHSEED='0',PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1',TMPDIR='/workspace/tmp'))
    dt=time.time()-t
    ru=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    print("%-7s rc=%d wall=%.1fs cpu=%.1fs out=%dKB err=%s" % (name,p.returncode,dt,ru.ru_utime+ru.ru_stime,len(p.stdout)//1024,p.stderr.decode()[:120]))
PYEOF
